name: nonApi_rptKennelRunStats
description: Generates a pivoted run-stats report for a kennel. Each hasher becomes a column; each run becomes a row. The 'paid' value encodes payment amount and type into a single integer so a single pivot covers both. Also inserts summary rows for total run counts and hare counts. The pivot column list is built dynamically from display names — dynamic SQL is required because the column count (one per hasher) is not known at compile time. Called by the portal or internal tools for reporting; not called by the API directly. Called (EXEC) by HC6.hcportal_rptKennelRunStats and by operators; not reachable by name through the shim. Wrapped in TRY/CATCH on 2026-09-23: a runtime error is logged to HC.ErrorLog and re-raised, so a nightly failure is diagnosable rather than only a Logic App / Function "Failed".

parameters.name: kennelId
parameters.description: The kennel to report on. All events, hashers, and payments are scoped to this kennel.

rowsets.name: PivotedRunStats
rowsets.description: Dynamic pivot: one row per event (ordered by Event_date DESC), plus two sentinel summary rows per hasher appended at the bottom (Event_name = 'Run totals' at future date 1/1/2200, 'Times hared' at 1/1/2100). Fixed columns are Event_name, Run_number, Total_hashers, Event_date. Dynamic columns: one per hasher named by their DisplayName, plus a 'Visitors & Virgins' aggregate column. Column order is by run count descending. The pivot cell value is an encoded integer representing payment + type + hare status. Schema cannot be fully defined statically.

columns.name: Event_name
columns.description: Effective event name — FbEventName or EventName depending on UseFbRunDetails. Summary rows use 'Run totals' or 'Times hared'.

columns.name: Run_number
columns.description: HC.Event.EventNumber for run rows. 0 for summary sentinel rows.

columns.name: Total_hashers
columns.description: Count of attendees (AttendenceState >= 20) for the event. NULL for summary sentinel rows.

columns.name: Event_date
columns.description: Effective event start datetime (CONVERT to datetime2). Summary rows use sentinel dates: '1/1/2200' (Run totals), '1/1/2100' (Times hared) to sort them after real events in DESC order.

columns.name: [HasherDisplayName] (dynamic)
columns.description: One column per unique hasher DisplayName, plus 'Visitors & Virgins'. Pivot cell value encodes: (COALESCE(DebitAmount * 10000, 99990000) + PaymentType + 100000000) * CASE WHEN isHare = 1 THEN -1 ELSE 1 END. Negative = hare, positive = not hare. Special payment sentinel 99990000 means no payment. Summary rows contain MAX(runcount) or MAX(hareCount) in the hasher's column.

codeSmells.issue: Dynamic SQL — the one exception to 'No dynamic SQL. Ever.'
codeSmells.detail: Lines 122–130 build the PIVOT statement as a string and run it with sp_executesql. T-SQL PIVOT needs its column list at compile time, so a per-hasher column cannot be done any other way; the identifiers are bracket-quoted with ']' doubled (line 116), so a display name cannot inject. Recorded as a smell because CLAUDE.md forbids dynamic SQL outright; this is the documented exception, not a licence.

codeSmells.issue: Raw HC.Event.EventStartDatetime used for Event_date, ordering and the running counts
codeSmells.detail: Lines 33, 39, 41, 70, 79, 90 use EventStartDatetime, the column with a spurious +00:00 on ~67% of rows (CLAUDE.md 'hc-event-datetimes': local clock ⇒ EventStartLocal; instant ⇒ EventStartDateTimeGmt). CONVERT(datetime2, …) strips the offset, so the report shows the stored wall clock, which is what a run-stats sheet wants — but the window ORDER BY mixes rows whose offset is real with rows whose offset is fake, so two runs on the same day can sort differently from the app's history, and the Visitors & Virgins join at line 79 matches on that converted value. Use EventStartLocal, which nonApi_updateRunCountsByUser already orders by, so the report's runcount agrees with the app's.

codeSmells.issue: Dynamic SQL column list escapes ']' via REPLACE — display names with ']' are safe
codeSmells.detail: The PIVOT column list wraps DisplayName in brackets using REPLACE(TRIM(@dname), ']', ']]') to escape any ']' characters before bracket-quoting. This follows the SQL Server convention for escaping bracket-delimited identifiers. Names containing ']' will appear with ']]' in the column header but the dynamic SQL will execute correctly.

codeSmells.issue: CURSOR used to build dynamic column list — O(N) cursor for N hashers
codeSmells.detail: The column list is assembled by iterating a CURSOR over all distinct hasher display names. This is the standard approach for dynamic PIVOT in SQL Server but is inherently serial. For kennels with many hashers, this adds latency proportional to hasher count. Downgraded to low (2026-10-13): a kennel has at most a few hundred distinct display names, so the cursor costs milliseconds; it does not bite in production.

codeSmells.issue: Encoded pivot cell value is opaque — complex decoding required by callers
codeSmells.detail: The pivot cell value encodes payment amount, payment type, and hare/non-hare status into a single integer using arithmetic encoding. Callers must implement the inverse formula to decode values, and the encoding assumes PaymentType fits in the low 4 digits, which is not enforced.

codeSmells.issue: Visitor/Virgin rows use a subquery with correlated scan against #rpt
codeSmells.detail: The Visitors & Virgins INSERT uses SELECT TOP 1 Total_hashers FROM #rpt WHERE t.Event_date = ... to look up the attendee count for each event. This is a correlated subquery executed once per event row. For kennels with many events it may be slow. An indexed join would be more efficient.

codeSmells.issue: Sentinel dates for summary rows ('1/1/2200', '1/1/2100') are implicit sort trick
codeSmells.detail: Summary rows are sorted to the bottom of the DESC-ordered result by using far-future dates. This is a clever trick but brittle — any caller that sorts or filters by Event_date must understand these sentinels represent non-event rows.

@kennelId has no SQL default. Run by operators / internal reporting, never through the shim. A call that omits one fails before the body runs — no HC.ErrorLog row, no graceful check (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default').

breakingChanges: HC5 source was HC.nonApi_rptKennelRunStats. HC6 migrates to HC6 schema with no functional changes to the pivot logic.
